title: The counit respects transported constants and product operations
statement: Let L:D→C be left adjoint to V:C→D between Cartesian monoidal categories, with V preserving finite products. For o:1_C→A, the composite L(!;terminalComparison(V)⁻¹;V(o));ε_A is !;o. For o:A×B→X and x:T→V(A),y:T→V(B), the composite L(⟨x,y⟩;productComparison(V)⁻¹;V(o));ε_X equals ⟨L(x);ε_A,L(y);ε_B⟩;o. The binary-operation specialization has A=B=X.

source.place: Sites, Section 00YR, finite-product transport; categorical naturality calculation for the ring and module operations in Modules on Sites, Tag 03CR.

proof.text: Naturality of the counit at o moves o outside the final counit. For a constant, both remaining maps have terminal codomain, hence are equal. For a product operation, compose the remaining maps with each projection. Naturality of the counit at the projection and the inverse comparison projection equations reduce both to L(x);ε_A or L(y);ε_B. Product extensionality gives equality.

proof_origin.place: Explicit Lean construction and operation calculations, expanding the transport details omitted in Tag 03CR.

mathlib_searches.query: A product preserving adjunction preserves ring operations and induces pushforward on sheaves of modules
mathlib_searches.results: SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardAdj, SheafOfModules.pushforward, SheafOfModules.PullbackConstruction.adjunction: these require a continuous functor of sites, rather than an arbitrary adjunction of sheaf categories.

mathlib_searches.verdict: Only scheme and continuous-site specializations were returned. Used the existing library finite-product and sectionwise constructions instead.

mathlib_searches.verdict: Use these projection identities to prove the new compatibility lemmas; no exact interface already exists.

from.place: Detailed form, strict-tower pullback: transporting ring and module structures across the finite-limit replacement sites.

lean.statement: theorem counit_pair {A B X : C} (o : A ⊗ B ⟶ X) {T : D} (x : T ⟶ V.obj A) (y : T ⟶ V.obj B) : L.map (lift x y ≫ (prodComparisonIso V A B).inv ≫ V.map o) ≫ adj.counit.app X = lift (L.map x ≫ adj.counit.app A) (L.map y ≫ adj.counit.app B) ≫ o
